newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Foster's shares fall after BHP deal.
newsitem.headline: Foster's shares fall after BHP deal.

text.p: Shares in Foster's Brewing Group Ltd slid 11.9 cents or 4.5 percent to A$2.481 on Friday, their lowest level since January 2, as trading resumed after Thursday's announcement of a share buyback and the sale by major shareholder The Broken Hill Proprietary Co of most of its stake.
On Thursday Foster's said BHP would place 86 percent of its 716.6 million share stake in Foster's to institutions at A$2.49 per share with the other 100 million shares offered to BHP shareholders.

The second part of the restructuring would see Foster's buy back 254.5 million of its shares from Japanese brewer Asahi Breweries for A$625 million, paying A$2.49 per share, which represents the bulk of Asahi's 270.3 million shareholding.

The 671.7 million shares, worth A$1.67 billion, were specialled through the market in four parcels prior to the market opening on Friday morning by Were Stockbroking and ABN Amro Hoare Govett (Securities).
The shares, all at A$2.49 each, went through in two parcels of 308.3 million shares, one of 32.5 million and one of 22.6 million.
Brokers said with the imminent availability of so many shares at A$2.49 each, some adjustment was inevitable.
"We're seeing investors take into account the huge onslaught of scrip onto the market," said dealer Scott Mailer of Daiwa Securities.
BHP's shares were slightly lower in a flat market, losing 11 cents to A$18.72 by 10.40 a.m. (0035 GMT).

Mailer said it was difficult to ascertain the precise value of the restructuring move to BHP, although he noted that BHP's recent signals that it was intensifying its focus on core bussiness meant the stake was obviously earmarked for sale.
"Management signalled a few weeks ago they were going to focus purely on core operations and clearly Foster's isn't a stategic fit for them," he said.
By 10.40 a.m. (0040 GMT), Foster's shares had recovered from their early lows to be seven cents lower at A$2.52 on turnover of 672.7 million shares.
